details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for at least isolated severe weather may increase across the area late this afternoon into evening. Convective trends are being monitored for a possible watch

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A thunderstorm has recently developed along the IA-MO border, near Centerville, IA along a residual outflow boundary that extends into west-central IL. A very moist boundary-layer exists in the vicinity of the surface front with dewpoints into the mid 70s to lower 80s, which are contributing to MLCAPE of 3000-3500+ J/kg, per latest objective analysis. Forcing associated with a remnant MCV may be contributing to the storm development with the current EAX VWP indicating 30-35 kt of westerly flow in the mid levels, suggestive of at least modest vertical shear. As such, some potential for isolated severe weather appears to exist, mainly in the form of locally damaging wind gusts, should sustained storms persist late this afternoon into evening

details.label: Summary
details.text: A conditional risk for isolated damaging wind gusts and perhaps a brief tornado exists across portions of far eastern Indiana into western Ohio. The need for a watch remains unclear

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Filtered diurnal heating downstream of an MCV readily apparent in observation data has allowed surface temperatures to warm into the low 80s F across portions of eastern IN/western OH, with latest objective analysis depicting around 1000 J/kg MLCAPE across this area. While some inhibition remains, deepening cumulus are noted in some areas of clearer skies. Recent CAM guidance continues to suggest that isolated thunderstorm development may occur in the next 1-3 hours across this region as ascent downstream of the approaching MCV continues to overspread the region. Should this occur, enhanced mid-level flow (sampled by the IND VWP) would be sufficient to support at least transient supercell structures should storms develop. In this scenario, poor low- and mid-level lapse rates would likely temper overall convective intensity, but modestly enhanced low-level shear and backing low-level flow (sampled by the ILN VWP) may support a conditional risk for isolated damaging wind gusts and perhaps a brief tornado. This scenario remains uncertain, but trends will continue to be monitored for potential watch issuance

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for severe storms capable of mainly severe wind gusts, potentially up to 70-80 mph, is expected to increase across the discussion area late this afternoon into evening. An additional watch is possible to the east/southeast of the recently issued severe thunderstorm watch 584 in effect across southeast Colorado

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Thunderstorms have developed along the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and adjacent Raton Mesa with a deepening cumulus field noted along a warm front from southwest KS into the OK and TX Panhandles. The 18Z DDC and AMA soundings modified for current surface conditions exhibit steep environmental lapse rates (especially in the low levels) with MLCAPE of 1500-2500 J/kg. Continued daytime heating should allow for further air mass destabilization with the strongest instability forecast north of the front from far southeast CO into southwest KS. Latest CAM guidance suggests the storms developing along the Sangre de Cristo Mountains will gradually grow upscale into one or multiple clusters later this afternoon into evening while moving/developing east into the High Plains. The recently issued severe thunderstorm watch 584 accounts for the large hail and severe wind gust potential with that regime. Additional storms will also be possible along the surface boundary from the northern TX into OK Panhandles and southwest KS, with some model signal for the separate regimes to merge across southwest KS this evening. Severe wind gusts, potentially up to 70-80 mph, appear to be the primary hazard with the latter regime, and convective trends are being monitored for an additional severe thunderstorm watch
